title: Hetmanate
summary: The Hetmanate refers to significant political entities in Ukrainian history, particularly the Cossack Hetmanate and the Ukrainian State, which are integral to the development of Ukraine's national identity and governance.

sections.heading: Cossack Hetmanate
paragraphs: The [[cossack-hetmanate|Cossack Hetmanate]], known in [[ukrainian|Ukrainian]] as Гетьманат, was a Ukrainian Cossack state that existed from 1649 to 1764. This political entity played a crucial role in the [[history-of-ukraine|history of Ukraine]], representing a period of autonomy and governance by Cossack leaders.

sections.heading: Ukrainian State
paragraphs: The [[ukrainian-state|Ukrainian State]], which is sometimes referred to as the Second Hetmanate, emerged in 1918. This entity marked a significant moment [[coal-in-ukraine|in Ukraine]]'s quest for independence and self-determination during the tumultuous period following World War I.

sections.heading: Political Context
paragraphs: The term '[[hetman|Hetman]]' denotes a political title that has historical significance in Central and [[eastern-europe|Eastern Europe]], particularly in the context of leadership within the Cossack communities of [[ukraine|Ukraine]]. This title is closely associated with the governance structures of the Hetmanate.
